text:
We piloted an AI note-taker with our field sales team for one quarter. Here's what we learned.

**1. Reps got time back.** Post-call admin dropped from about 25 minutes to under 10. That meant more selling, less typing in the parking lot.

**2. CRM data got better.** Notes were consistent, so managers finally saw next steps and objections in one place.

**3. Trust took work.** Some customers hesitated at first. Asking consent upfront, and explaining how notes were stored, turned most "maybe" answers into "sure."

**4. Summaries aren't strategy.** The tool captured what was said. Reps still had to decide what mattered.

**5. Coaching improved.** Managers used call snippets in 1:1s instead of relying on memory.

Our takeaway: AI handles the record. People handle the relationship.

What did your team learn from piloting AI tools?
